newsitem.title: UK: UK union confirms call for 4.42 stg/hr minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: UK union confirms call for 4.42 stg/hr minimum wage.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government should set a minimum wage of 4.42 pounds an hour, Rodney Bickerstaffe, the general secretary of Britain's largest trade union, UNISON, said on Thursday.
Bickerstaffe, repeating his union's argument that the minumum wage promised by Labour should be set at half the median male salary, said the 4.42 pounds level represented a fair rate.

Labour, sensitive to charges a minimum wage could cost jobs, has refused to detail a rate. Instead it has set up a Low Pay Commission to take evidence from workers' and employers' bodies before recommending a minimum wage rate.
Bickerstaffe said in an article in the New Statesman: "But 19 million British workers already get 4.42 pounds an hour and the country has not sunk under the waves.
"Why should it, then, if an extra five million adults who earn less than 4.42 pounds have their pay brought up to a decent threshold." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
